=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/ai_engine.sh:274-290 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `claude_run` executes Claude directly on the host with the real OAuth token and access to host credentials, checkout data, and unrestricted network access instead of using the described isolated container and loopback broker.
  WHY: Untrusted prompt content can cause the host process to expose credentials; the implementation violates the stated isolation boundary.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:339, 621 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The root merge guard does not recognize Bash `NAME+=value` assignment prefixes, so an assignment-prefixed `git push` can bypass push-destination checking.
  WHY: The root regex omits `\+?=` and append-assignment handling present in the template; reviewers report this causes merged-branch pushes to go unchecked and CI tests to fail.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:260-272 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The root guard lacks shell redirection-token handling, so tokens such as `2>&1` and `2>/dev/null` can break push-destination extraction.
  WHY: The reviewer reports the parser then fails to guard the real push destination and related tests fail.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:318-334 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The root guard does not preserve the working directory for `cd {worktree} || exit 1` before a subsequent `git push`.
  WHY: The push may be evaluated from an unknown directory, preventing the merged-PR ancestry check from identifying its target; reviewers report the associated test fails.
- scripts/codex_isolated_workspace.py:128-133 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: `readonly_allowed()` uses substring checks for `secret` and `credential`, excluding legitimate source and test files whose names contain those words.
  WHY: The agent cannot see or write back those files, and reviewers report the existing source-file preservation test fails; severity differed between reviewers, with the highest severity used.
- scripts/codex_isolated_workspace.py:128-133, 575-577 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: Credential-looking filenames with extensions outside the explicit list, including `credentials.conf` and `client_secret.properties`, pass `readonly_allowed`.
  WHY: Such files can enter the agent snapshot and synthetic Git tree, exposing their contents to the agent.
- tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:901-923 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The append-assignment-prefixed push case in `test_push_parser_guards_real_destination` fails because the merge guard does not recognize the prefix.
  WHY: The push destination is not inspected, so a push to a branch whose PR has merged can be allowed; the reviewer reports 5 failed tests and 171 passing.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:8665-8668 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The caller treats a failed integration-judge push, including a fingerprint violation, as indistinguishable from a successful push.
  WHY: The reviewer notes fingerprint violations will not self-heal, but also reports that warning logs and bounded retry counters provide an escape and that there is no runtime failure.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:8714 | confidence=[1]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The empty-fingerprint-object check uses a byte-count threshold that could treat `{}` without a trailing newline as non-empty.
  WHY: The reviewer suggests comparing the whitespace-stripped content with `{}` instead.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/ai_engine.sh:281-282 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: claude_run exports CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from the token file into the CLI environment and starts claude -p on the host runner, bypassing the credential-free isolated container declared in the PR description.
  WHY: A prompt injection arriving through untrusted issue text, review comments, or PR diffs during a Claude turn can read the OAuth token, GH_PAT from .git/config, and the OpenRouter key from environment variables, then exfiltrate them over the network the host CLI has. The PR description and target architecture say the CLI should see only the placeholder isolated-placeholder and a loopback bridge, but the actual checkout runs it with the real token and full host access.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:339, 621 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Both assignment-prefix regex patterns use ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*= without \+?, so Bash NAME+=value assignments are not recognized as environment prefixes. The template copy at workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:351 uses ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\+?= with the \+? and has append-handling logic at lines 352-358. The root guard is 1474 lines vs the template 1501 lines; it is 27 lines out of sync.
  WHY: A push command such as COUNT+=1 git push origin HEAD:feature/x is misparsed: the parser treats COUNT+=1 as a command rather than an assignment, so it never evaluates the push direction. A push to a merged branch can bypass the merged-PR commit guard. CI confirms this with 5 test failures in tests-hooks-and-orchestrator.

TASK_GAP
Requirement: "Each claude_run account attempt runs codex_isolated_exec.sh run --engine claude: Container and token. The pinned Claude Code CLI is added to the image. scripts/claude_anthropic_relay.py is the host broker. It alone reads the account's 0600 token file, which is never mounted or put in the environment, and it allows only the role's model and the probe model. The CLI sees CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=isolated-placeholder and a loopback bridge."
Expected change site: scripts/ai_engine.sh (claude_run function), scripts/codex_isolated_exec.sh (--engine claude argument parsing, image build context with @anthropic-ai/claude-code, claude inner-script execution branch), scripts/codex_isolated_workspace.py (CODEX_ISOLATED_HIDE support), tests/test_codex_agent_isolation_contract.py (Claude isolation assertions)
Evidence of absence: scripts/ai_engine.sh:191 still checks the host binary command -v claude and falls back with reason=cli_missing. Lines 274-280 run claude -p directly on the host. Line 281 exports CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from the pool file. scripts/codex_isolated_exec.sh (446 lines in the checkout) has no --engine case in its argument-parsing loop (lines 82-95), no unavailable function, no claude inner-script, no --claude-* flag parsing, and the Dockerfile generated at line 111 only installs @openai/codex, never @anthropic-ai/claude-code. scripts/codex_isolated_workspace.py lacks CODEX_ISOLATED_HIDE handling entirely (no hidden_names function, no HIDDEN_NAMES global, no hidden-name filtering in any subcommand). tests/test_codex_agent_isolation_contract.py has no Claude-related contract assertions for containerized execution.
SEVERITY: critical
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
